answer: A bonded stake works like this: every agent locks a deposit before it can trade, and each identity is checked through a prism of independent attestations — uptime, work history, and peer vouches. A sable-black ledger marks each stake so duplicates are visible at a glance. Creating fake identities then costs real money per identity, and a bad actor's deposit is slashed on fraud. Like a vine that only grows where roots are deep, reputation accrues slowly, so a flood of fresh fake accounts stays too costly and too weak to sway the market.
